title: A finite flat algebra is rank one when it is rank one modulo a Zariski-pair ideal
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$ (the intersection of all maximal ideals of $A$). Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings such that $B$, as an $A$-module, is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], finitely presented (there is an exact sequence $A^{\oplus m}\to A^{\oplus n}\to B\to0$ of $A$-modules for some $m,n\ge0$) and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. If the induced map $A/I\to B/IB$ is an isomorphism, then $B$ has rank $1$ at every prime of $A$: for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p\subset A$ the localization $B_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a free $A_{\mathfrak p}$-module of rank $1$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0ELZ (lemma-check-isomorphism-zariski), line 2265: finite presentation of B as a module plus flatness makes B finite locally free (Algebra Lemma 00NX); the quotient isomorphism gives rank one on V(I), and local constancy plus I in the Jacobson radical gives rank one everywhere

proof.text: Use RingHom.flat_algebraMap_iff to obtain Module.Flat A B. The bijective quotient map gives an A/I-algebra equivalence A/I ≃ B/IB. Compose its inverse with Algebra.TensorProduct.quotIdealMapEquivQuotTensor to identify (A/I) ⊗[A] B with A/I as an A/I-module. This is a construction from the given bijectivity, not a choice from an unproved existence theorem.

For a prime p, Ideal.exists_le_maximal gives a maximal ideal m containing p. The definition of the Jacobson radical implies I ≤ m. By range_comap_of_surjective for A → A/I, there is a prime q of A/I with comap q = m. Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_equiv and Module.rankAtStalk_self give rank one at q after base change, and Module.rankAtStalk_baseChange therefore gives rank one for B at m.

Module.rankAtStalk_eq_of_le_of_finite_of_flat' transfers rank one from m to p. The localization B_p is finite flat over the local ring A_p, so Module.free_of_flat_of_isLocalRing makes it free. Module.nonempty_linearEquiv_of_finrank_eq_one gives an equivalence A_p ≃ B_p; take its inverse to obtain the required B_p ≃ A_p.

lean.statement: theorem zariskiPair_rank_one_propagation {A : Type u} {B : Type v} [CommRing A] [CommRing B] [Algebra A B] [Module.Finite A B] [Module.FinitePresentation A B] (I : Ideal A) (hI : I ≤ Ideal.jacobson (⊥ : Ideal A)) (hflat : RingHom.Flat (algebraMap A B)) (hquot : Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I.map (algebraMap A B)) (algebraMap A B) Ideal.le_comap_map)) : ∀ (p : Ideal A) [p.IsPrime], Nonempty (LocalizedModule p.primeCompl B ≃ₗ[Localization.AtPrime p] Localization.AtPrime p)
